Subject: FintechCo - deployment mode & security follow-up

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the outstanding items we promised to follow up on: 

Summary of current constraints (from your security & infra team):
- SSO: Okta SAML required for identity (SCIM optional).
- Key management: BYOK required; goal is customer-owned keys (KMS/HSM).
- Logging: 7-year retention requirement for audit logs; must be exportable to customer-managed storage.
- Data residency: US-only tenancy for production.

How this maps to Redwood deployment modes (initial thoughts):
- Hosted API: easiest to stand up but typically does not meet BYOK/HSM/long-term retention requirements.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with stronger isolation; supports customer KMS (BYOK) for encryption at-rest and Okta SAML; logging retention can be extended via export but default retention is shorter.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control over networking, direct KMS/HSM integration (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM), and you control log retention and storage lifecycle.

Next steps / asks for your team:
1) Can you confirm whether BYOK via AWS KMS is sufficient, or do you require an on-prem HSM?
2) Who from your security team should we include on the architecture workshop (we recommend both infra and compliance leads)?
3) Preferred week for a 60-min architecture + procurement session (proposed windows below).

I've attached a draft mutual action plan (Draft_MAP_v2.docx) with proposed milestones and timelines.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through details.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear notes. Quick technical summary to help distinguish the options and call out what requires Professional Services / Engineering support: 

1) Hosted API (Redwood-managed):
- Pros: fastest to launch, lowest setup effort.
- Cons: does not meet BYOK/HSM requirements or long-term external log storage by default. Not recommended for regulated workloads.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity in Redwood tenancy):
- Isolation: Dedicated GPU pools logically isolated for your account.
- KMS/HSM: Supports BYOK via cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). We can accept customer CMKs; for CloudHSM-level guarantees we integrate with AWS KMS-backed HSM (CloudHSM).
- SSO: Okta SAML and SCIM provisioning supported.
- Logging: default retention in Redwood's logging stack is typically 90 days; however, we provide configurable exports (e.g., continuous export to your S3 or to a SIEM). Export setup and validation are part of the onboarding PS scope.
- Effort: faster than Private, less infra work, but some PS required to configure KMS/SCIM and log export.

3) Private (VPC or on-prem package):
- Isolation: customer-controlled VPC, private control plane option; can be deployed into your AWS account or on-prem.
- KMS/HSM: full BYOK + direct CloudHSM integration or passthrough to an on-prem HSM is supported. We typically work with your security team to validate key wrapping and HSM attestation.
- SSO: direct IdP integration inside your network (Okta SAML + SCIM) with no external traffic.
- Logging: you control storage and lifecycle; we can stream audit + request logs to your S3 with 7+ year retention.
- Effort: highest implementation effort and costs (platform licensing + deployment + ongoing ops ownership).

Recommended next steps:
- Architecture workshop (60 minutes) with your infra & security to confirm CloudHSM vs on-prem HSM approach, S3 bucket policies, and network egress rules.
- During workshop we'll capture the exact list of logs (audit, request traces, application logs) and define the export pipeline and retention lifecycle.
- Post-workshop: we can produce an SOW and a high-level timeline (typical Private delivery 8-12 weeks depending on availability of security approvals).

Relevant docs: https://redwood.app/docs/deployment-private-vs-dedicated (overview), and I'll share the SOC2 packet in a separate email to your security contact.

-Let me know preferred times for the workshop and we will block time.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
